Fix session worktree lifecycle: remove worktree before merge attempt to prevent orphaned branches and manual cleanup
context: Current flow in runWithSessionWorktreeWithConflictSettings (cmd/gromit/interactive_worktree.go): session ends → record pending branch → attempt immediate merge → clearMergedState removes worktree + deletes branch only on success. Bug: if immediate merge fails (run loop is doing concurrent git ops), the session worktree stays alive and checked out on its branch (e.g. gromit/review-<timestamp>). git branch -d silently fails if that branch is checked out in any worktree. So the run loop deferred path (internal/runner/lifecycle.go ~line 377, PendingBranches loop) calls MergeBack, which can merge successfully but cannot delete the branch — it persists, the worktree directory orphans, and this repeats every run loop iteration. Fix 1: call git worktree remove <sessionDir> BEFORE the merge attempt, not after, so the branch is never held when merge+delete runs — whether via the immediate path or the run loop deferred path. Fix 2: the run loop MergeBack (internal/worktree/worktree.go) only deletes the branch, not the worktree directory — it needs to also clean up orphaned session worktree dirs whose branch was just merged. User symptom: terminal merge-conflict errors immediately after every interactive session (retro/review/explore/refine/debug/plan), then persistent orphaned branches requiring manual git worktree remove + git branch -d.

If format.go grows further — e.g., when phase-cost-optimization adds per-phase display sections — extracting into internal/runner/display/ or internal/status/ would maintain the <550 line production file rule and improve package cohesion. The formatting functions (formatRun, formatHealth, formatSPCSummary, formatModelPerformance, formatRecommendation, formatPipeline, formatDuration, formatSPCLine, formatSPCValue, simplifySPCMetric, formatEscalationBreakdown, formatRecurrenceBreakdown, formatReliabilityLine, formatRunningLine, formatElapsedSuffix, formatIterationPrefix, formatItems) form a natural unit that could become a display/formatting package. Not urgent at 389/550 lines, but worth revisiting after phase-cost-optimization lands. Context: discovered during thorough review of cumulative changes across 9 debug/build/refactor iterations on 2026-02-22.

debug --model flag is Claude-only: shouldOverrideDebugModel() returns false for non-Claude agents, and the override always creates a Claude agent. Either make --model work for all agents or document the limitation clearly.
selectLearningsProvider() in constructor.go prefers providers["claude"] for learnings filtering — should pick the first available provider or use a config preference instead of hardcoding Claude bias

Gate integration tests in gate_test.go test mock behavior, not real decomposerAdapter. The 4 new 'integration' tests (EndToEnd, RecordsOutput, ClosesParentBead, FullIntegration) each create local adapter implementations mimicking decomposerAdapter rather than using the real one from constructor_adapters.go. If decomposerAdapter.Decompose() changes, these tests won't catch the regression. Consider (a) testing through the real adapter by extracting testable logic, or (b) renaming tests to accurately describe them as gate-level scope-gate contract tests. Needs design discussion on whether gate_test.go should import runner types (dependency cycle risk) or whether testing the Decomposer interface contract is sufficient.

Define product-level policy for decomposition failure semantics: current behavior falls back to Block on decomposition errors, but partial decomposition and retry behavior are not formally specified. Clarify whether failures should block, error, or degrade to proceed, and how operators should recover.
